A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DARTS-TS research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables, and figures, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting experiments on twelve datasets, efficiency measurements, architecture examples, and window-size and component ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds sampled-architecture analyses, foundation-model comparisons, statistical results, and further ablations.

M1.justification: The proposed hierarchical search space, operation sets, forecasting heads, weighted Flat/Seq combination, differentiable search, and perturbation-based hierarchical pruning remain unchanged. Newly evaluated ablation variants and expanded implementation disclosures do not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same twelve datasets: four ETT datasets, ECL, Traffic, Weather, Exchange, and four PEMS datasets. New analyses and foundation-model comparisons reuse this coverage; they do not introduce a new forecasting domain or task.

E2.justification: V2 adds actual accuracy and efficiency comparisons against TimesFM and Moirai-MoE in Appendix D, Tables 11-12, and Figure 11. The original seven forecasting baselines remain. The component comparison also gains DARTS-TS CV and Concat Seq First controls in Table 13.

E3.justification: New protocols include sampling 3,000 architectures, a five-fold cross-validation control, horizon and optimization-epoch sweeps, and batch-one foundation-model timing. Appendix B also reports PEMS look-back windows of 96 instead of v1's 336 and specifies AdamW for small-dataset retraining rather than v1's blanket Adam description. V2 Section 6.1 still states 336 for all models, so the PEMS implementation and whether existing experiments were rerun remain unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's window-size and macro-component ablations, v2 adds search-space performance distributions, cross-dataset architecture comparisons, zero-cost-proxy correlations, and operation-presence analyses. Appendix E adds horizon transfer, cross-validation, reversed component ordering, optimization-duration sensitivity, operation removal, RevIN removal, and matched versus mixed encoder-decoder controls.

E5.justification: V1 already reports five-seed means and standard deviations and marks statistical comparability through underlining. V2 substantially expands this reporting with explicit statistics and p-values against selected best baselines in Tables 9-10 and a stated 0.05 significance threshold. The test itself is not named. Existing five-run counts remain unchanged; the new foundation-model evaluations explicitly use one seed.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-2 and the corresponding detailed benchmark tables are retained. V2 adds substantial new results for search-space analyses, foundation models, statistical comparisons, and ablations. Existing ECL efficiency entries also change: v1 Figure 4 reports DARTS-TS inference at 29 ms and 145 MB with 1.21 million parameters; v2 Figure 8 reports 20 ms and 119 MB with 0.831 million parameters. These are revised measurements, not an established gain for an unchanged model.

T1.justification: The forecasting formulation, bilevel optimization problem, weighted prediction equation, operation definitions, and forecasting-loss formulas retain their mathematical content. V2's additional proxy and architecture discussions are empirical or intuitive; no new theorem, proof, or substantive formal derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: V1 presents DARTS-TS as a proposed differentiable NAS framework. V2 centers novelty on the hierarchical search space and describes DARTS-TS as architectures obtained by applying existing DARTS-PT. Its contribution list also adds the claim that this search space has distinctive properties and challenges relative to CNN-based NAS spaces. The lightweight, competitive forecasting claim remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations linking heterogeneous operations to weak zero-cost proxies, dataset-dependent architecture performance to task-specific search and transferable priors, and mixed operations to efficiency without explicitly optimizing latency. Appendix D qualifies TimesFM comparisons through reported training-data overlap. New ablation discussions address overfitting and component dependence; the original distribution-shift limitation remains.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents optimizer hyperparameters, search/training epoch budgets, gradient clipping, learning-rate restarts, and per-stage GPU costs in Appendix B. It clarifies rolling-origin evaluation and exclusion of test data from search, and provides foundation-model checkpoints, hardware, runtime limits, and sampling settings. The project repository link remains, while v1's separate baseline-license list is removed.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around NAS benchmarks and zero-cost proxies, adding works such as NAS-Bench-Suite-Zero, SNIP, and SynFlow. It also introduces references concerning operation importance, prior-informed search, multi-objective NAS, and Moirai-MoE. Together with the revised contribution framing, these additions position the work more explicitly as a heterogeneous search-space contribution using existing optimization methods.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most retained explanatory prose persist. V2 copyedits grammar and terminology, switches to author-year citations, revises the contribution list, inserts new analytical subsections, and reorganizes the appendices. The broader-impact and license sections are removed; the existing narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: V2 adds distribution plots, proxy-correlation and horizon heatmaps, operation analyses, epoch-sensitivity plots, and foundation-model and encoder-decoder comparisons, alongside new cost, hyperparameter, significance, and ablation tables. The journal format changes the title block, headers, sizing, and placement. Existing architecture examples and the window-size heatmap are retained. Expanded Table 13 contains duplicated Flat Only metric columns.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the evidence for the central heterogeneous search-space contribution through systematic architecture sampling and targeted operation, encoder-decoder, and search-setting controls. Detailed hyperparameters, search costs, and explicit statistical results also address important reproducibility and evidential gaps in v1. The conflicting PEMS window descriptions, unspecified statistical test, and Table 13 formatting error limit clarity, but the stronger validation and technical documentation provide a substantial net quality improvement.
